name: Evacuation Drill at the Fulfilment Centre
description:
During a fire drill, the floor of an Amazon fulfilment centre is a grid of r rows and c columns. Each cell is:
'.' open floor
'#' a rack (nobody can enter it)
'E' an exit
'P' a person (the cell is open floor with a person standing on it)

Every person walks to their nearest exit, moving one cell up, down, left or right each second. People never block each other. Print the number of seconds until the last person who can escape reaches an exit (0 if nobody can escape), and the number of people who cannot reach any exit.

Input: The first line has two integers r and c. Each of the next r lines is a string of c characters from '.', '#', 'E', 'P'.
Output: Two integers separated by a space: the seconds, then the number of people who cannot escape.

Constraints:
- 1 <= r, c <= 200
- There can be zero or more exits and zero or more people

Amazon OA pattern: multi-source BFS on a grid.

test_cases.description: The top-right exit is boxed in by racks, so everyone uses the bottom-left exit: the three people need 3, 4 and 6 seconds. The last one arrives after 6 seconds and nobody is stuck: 6 0.
The right-hand area has no exit, so both people there are stuck; nobody escapes, so the time is 0: 0 2.

name: Sealed Zones in the Warehouse
description:
A safety inspector checks a warehouse floor drawn as a grid of r rows and c columns. Each cell is:
'.' open floor
'#' a rack wall
'W' a worker (open floor with a worker on it)
'E' an exit (open floor)

A zone is a group of non-rack cells joined by moves up, down, left and right. A zone is sealed if it contains at least one worker but no exit.

Print three numbers:
1. the number of sealed zones,
2. the total number of workers in sealed zones,
3. the shortest walking distance (in moves) from any worker to any exit, over all workers who can reach an exit, or -1 if no worker can reach an exit.

Input: The first line has two integers r and c. Each of the next r lines is a string of c characters from '.', '#', 'W', 'E'.
Output: Three integers separated by spaces.

Constraints:
- 1 <= r, c <= 200
- There can be zero or more workers and zero or more exits

Amazon OA pattern: connected components (flood fill) plus multi-source BFS on a grid.

test_cases.description: Zones (cells joined up/down/left/right, racks excluded): the top-left zone has a worker and no exit, so it is sealed (1 zone, 1 worker). The rest is one zone with an exit; its nearest worker to an exit is (1,3), 2 steps away. Answer: 1 1 2.
Each worker is alone in a 1-cell zone with no exit, so 3 sealed zones with 3 workers, and no worker can reach an exit: 3 3 -1.

name: Delivery Vans With Cleaning Time
description:
An Amazon Fresh hub plans n refrigerated delivery trips for tomorrow. Trip i starts at minute s and ends at minute e (the van is busy from s up to e). After every trip, a van must be cleaned for exactly c minutes before it can start another trip, so a van that ends a trip at minute e is free again at minute e + c, and can start a trip that begins at minute e + c or later.

Print the minimum number of vans needed to run all n trips.

Input: The first line has two integers n and c. Each of the next n lines has two integers s and e.
Output: A single integer, the minimum number of vans.

Constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 100000
- 0 <= c <= 1000000000
- 0 <= s < e <= 1000000000
- e + c can exceed the 32-bit integer range

Amazon OA pattern: sorting + sweep line / heap over intervals.

test_cases.description: Van A does 0-5 and is clean at 7, so it can do 7-10 (clean at 12) and then 12-14. The 6-8 trip starts while van A is still being cleaned, so it needs van B. 2 vans.
With no cleaning time, one van ends a trip exactly when the next one starts, so 1 van does all three.

name: Longest Uptime Between Maintenance Windows
description:
An AWS server is watched for one day, from minute 0 to minute T. The operations team has scheduled n maintenance windows; during window i the server is down from minute l to minute r. Windows may overlap or touch. At every other moment of the day the server is up.

Print two numbers: the length of the longest continuous up-time within [0, T] (0 if the server is never up), and the number of separate up-time gaps whose length is at least L minutes.

Input: The first line has three integers n, T and L. Each of the next n lines has two integers l and r.
Output: Two integers separated by a space.

Constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 100000
- 1 <= T <= 1000000000
- 1 <= L <= 1000000000
- 0 <= l < r <= T

Amazon OA pattern: sort + merge intervals, then scan the gaps.

test_cases.description: Down from 2 to 9 and from 15 to 17. Up-gaps: 0-2 (2), 9-15 (6), 17-24 (7). Longest is 7, and 2 gaps are at least 3 long. Answer: 7 2.
The two windows together cover the whole day 0-10, so there is no up-time at all: 0 0.
